name: eccentric-tube
why: A Ø20 tube 30 long with its Ø16 bore 1 mm off axis toward +X: pi * (100 - 64) * 30 = 3392.920 mm3, recorded 0.035% under as every volume here is, measured on the tessellation.. Along X through the axis the line crosses the tube at -10, the bore at -7 and 9, the tube at 10: a first wall of 3 and 4 mm in all. The wall is thinnest where the two circles are nearest, 10 - (8 + 1) = 1.000 between tube and bore, and grows as 2 - cos of the angle away from there, so the sampled minimum sits within a few microns of it.
